methods: Video (1352x760 px, 60 fps, 0.2 min; sha256 b2a2971df465) of 5 fishs in a 29 x 29 cm arena was analysed with Kappa 0.1.0 (protocol sha256 ea8d697e20bb, confirmed by Yehor Ivashchenko via the kappa command line). Each fish was segmented and tracked with sam3.1_multiplex@0567debeec80 (self-hosted, sam3@f1647e8d0c1d, kappa-sam v3) from the text prompt "fish", and positions were converted to centimetres with a four-point homography of the arena floor. Trajectories were smoothed with a median filter (0.2 s window). Zones were defined as a periphery band within 3 cm of the walls. A subject was counted inside a zone when its body centre was inside it. Of 26 reported values, 0 were verified, 26 were withheld because the underlying track failed an integrity check, and 0 were refused as not measurable.

body.notes: Modelled on the 3D-ZeF benchmark set-up seen from its top camera: a square tank of about 30 x 30 cm (an assumption; measure your tank and correct width_cm and height_cm). Positions are projected onto the water-surface plane, so swimming depth is ignored and distances are 2D. Near the walls means within 3 cm of a wall (about one adult body length), judged by the body centre. Inter-fish distance is the mean distance between every pair of fish, one value for the group. Five fish that touch often trade identities; each unresolved swap locks that fish's later numbers until a person marks who is who. arena.corners_px is null until the tank corners are marked on a frame.
body.question: How far does each fish swim, minute by minute, how long does each fish spend near the walls, and how far apart do the fish keep on average?

refused.reason: a top-view camera does not see depth, so bottom dwelling needs a side view
refused.request: time in the bottom third of the tank (the classic novel-tank diving measure)

body.title: Novel tank, five adult zebrafish, top view (3D-ZeF style)

findings.claim: No reportable behavioural numbers exist in this run: all 26 results (per-fish distance totals and 5-s bins, wall_time for subjects 1-5, and the group inter_fish_distance) are status locked with null values, verified=0 and locked=26 in the summary. Any distance, wall-time or inter-fish value quoted from this run would contradict the manifest itself.
findings.suggestion: Withhold all individual and group metrics until the blocking identity and counting events are resolved by a person, as the protocol notes require.

findings.claim: Individual identity is unresolved from very early in the clip and repeatedly thereafter. The first ambiguous contact is at frames 35-72 (contact:1-4:35), with further unresolved blocking swaps for almost every fish: contact:1-4:113, contact:1-4:198, contact:2-4:238, contact:1-2:292, contact:4-5:292, contact:2-5:333, contact:1-4:450, contact:2-4:553, contact:3-4:558, contact:2-3:568, contact:1-4:590, contact:3-5:611, contact:4-5:644 and contact:1-5:646. Keeping vs swapping identities fits within 1.1-1.9x vs the required 2.0x identity_margin, and resolved_by is null. Per the protocol notes each unresolved swap locks that fish's later numbers, so per-fish distance and wall_time cannot be attributed to subjects 1-5.
findings.suggestion: Manually confirm identities at each fix_frame, or terminate individual-level analysis at the first unresolved swap.

findings.claim: The expected count of 5 fish is not cleanly met. count_mismatch:scene:0 reports tracks 0, 3 and 4 present for frames 0-899 that are not among the expected subjects, with track 4 within a body length of subject 1 at frame 0. Additional unassigned tracks appear in count_mismatch:scene:216 (track 8, near subject 3), count_mismatch:scene:277 (track 9, near subject 1, frames 277-899) and count_mismatch:scene:378 (track 10, near subject 4, frames 378-899). It is unclear which detections are the five experimental fish, which are duplicates/false positives, and whether inter_fish_distance used the correct set of animals.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the extra tracks with the five expected subjects before any group or individual metric is released.

findings.claim: Two further blocking track failures are unresolved: subject 2 jumps 3.2 cm between frames 377-378 at 190 cm/s, above the protocol's own 150 cm/s max_speed limit (teleport:2:377), indicating a wrong-object jump or identity swap; and subject 4 disappears for the final 149 frames, 2.48 s, far beyond the 0.40 s maximum interpolated gap (gap:4:751, frames 751-900). Subject 4's totals and the full-15-s group inter-fish distance therefore cannot be computed as specified.
findings.suggestion: Inspect frame 378 for subject 2 and either recover subject 4 after frame 751 or truncate all group metrics to the common visible period.

findings.claim: The temporal design does not match the stated question or the paradigm. The protocol asks how far each fish swims 'minute by minute', but the video is only 15.0 s (900 frames at 60 fps) and distance uses bin_s=5.0, giving three 5-s bins (frames 0-300, 300-600, 600-900). A 15-s excerpt cannot support minute-by-minute reporting or the habituation-over-minutes analysis conventional to the novel-tank test.
findings.suggestion: Record/analyse a full multi-minute trial binned at 60 s as stated, or rewrite the question and claims to 5-s bins over 15 s.

findings.claim: Testing five zebrafish together departs from the conventional solitary novel-tank test: locomotion and wall proximity of each fish are confounded by shoaling/social interactions (the run itself records mean inter-fish distance and frequent contacts), and the five fish in one tank are not independent replicates. Per-fish distance/wall_time here cannot be read as standard individual novel-tank anxiety endpoints without addressing this.
findings.suggestion: Either run the novel-tank assay individually as conventionally defined, or reframe and analyse this explicitly as a group/shoaling assay with the tank as the unit of replication.

findings.claim: Absolute centimetre values rest on an unmeasured arena calibration. The protocol notes state the tank is 'about 30 x 30 cm (an assumption; measure your tank and correct width_cm and height_cm)', yet the protocol uses 29.0 x 29.0 cm and the methods paragraph presents 'a 29 x 29 cm arena' as fact. Every cm distance, the 150 cm/s teleport threshold and the 3 cm near_wall band scale directly with this assumption, so an error propagates proportionally into distance, wall_time and inter_fish_distance.
findings.suggestion: Measure the actual tank, document the calibration and its error, and correct width_cm/height_cm before reporting absolute values.

findings.claim: This top-view run cannot deliver the classic novel-tank diving measure. The protocol itself refused 'time in the bottom third of the tank (the classic novel-tank diving measure)' because a top-view camera does not see depth, and the notes confirm positions are projected onto the water-surface plane with swimming depth ignored. The methods statement that positions were converted 'with a four-point homography of the arena floor' is inconsistent with that water-surface projection and leaves depth/parallax error unquantified. Claims framed as a standard novel-tank diving/anxiety assay are not supported; at most this is 2D locomotion and wall proximity.
findings.suggestion: Add a synchronised side view for bottom-dwelling/diving, and state the projection plane and parallax treatment consistently.

findings.claim: The near_wall definition is a high-coverage, threshold-sensitive zone that needs justification and chance-level context before it can be read as thigmotaxis: a 3 cm periphery band in a 29 x 29 cm arena covers about 37% of the arena area (1 - 23x23 / 29x29), entry is by body centroid with min_dwell_s=0.0, so momentary centroid crossings count fully. Wall-time conclusions will change materially with band width or dwell rule, and no sensitivity analysis or chance expectation is provided.
findings.suggestion: Justify the 3 cm/centroid/zero-dwell rule, report the zone area fraction/chance level, and show robustness to plausible band widths.

findings.claim: The methods paragraph is not fully supported by the record and omits information needed to interpret or replicate the assay. It gives only count and arena size (as '5 fishs', without even restating zebrafish/adult status from the protocol title): no strain, age, sex, body size, housing, acclimation/handling, water depth, lighting or testing-time information appears anywhere in the manifest. It also describes the clip as '0.2 min' whereas the video record is 15.0 s (0.25 min), a discrepancy that matters because all per-bin distances depend on the analysed window.
findings.suggestion: Correct the duration and species wording, and add standard animal, housing, acclimation and environmental details to the methods.

withheld: Locked and refused results carry no value, evidence or uncertainty here, and behaviour bouts are listed only for a subject whose every result for that behaviour is verified: a locked number is not defensible until its integrity events are settled, and a locked count is just its bouts counted. The full manifest kept for audit is the file at `path`, sha256 `manifest_sha256`.
